info.title: Plan
info.description: Run a plan page. A plan is a page whose title ends in Plan or Roadmap; its phases are headings, its checkpoints are task lines, one per markdown item, and its Open Questions are task lines holding a red question link. The Plan Tool reads all of that in the browser; the operations here are the services that write. Update Plan is the mechanical one: deterministic, no model call, written in place. Do Next Phase and Revise Plan are the agentic ones: they ask the shared Claude door and answer with a job whose report the tool opens as a ghost page; they write nothing to any page. Revise Plan's ghost has the plan's own title and carries the whole page; Save over the plan (saveRevision) writes it over the plan in place through the journal, so the version replaced is the plan's _rev<N>. Rewind writes nothing: the tool opens the _rev the journal holds as a ghost beside the plan, and forking it is the rewind. Revise Site is agentic too: it reads every answered question and every page of the site and asks the door for a Revision Proposal, a job that writes nothing; Go Ahead, applyRevision, then rewrites the pages that proposal names one at a time through the door, the plan last. Finish Plan is mechanical too: once every checkpoint is ticked it writes the plan's Conclusion section with its demo link. Red-link finds the plan's links that have no page behind them on this farm, question links and the Open Questions section left alone, and as a job researches each on the web through the door (WebSearch and WebFetch only) and writes its page, a new page with one journaled create each.

post.summary: Update Plan: tick the questions whose pages now exist and re-render the plan's markdown asset
post.description: Reads the plan page on this site. Every unticked Open Questions line, - [ ] [[Question?]] gloss, whose question now has a page on this site or on a sibling site of this farm is ticked, with one journal edit per item ticked, and the page is written whole (temp file and rename). When the plan links a page titled Open Questions on this site (a research site keeps its questions there, linked from the plan's See section), that page is read whole and ticked by the same rule, journaled on that page, not the plan. The site's sitemap.json, site-index.json and sitemap.xml are then removed together so it reindexes on the next request. The plan's markdown is re-rendered to assets/<slug>/<slug>.md either way. The write holds the farm WIP marker (~/.wiki-hosting/AGENT-WIP.json, the wiki-wip protocol) and releases it; a live claim by anyone else is answered with 409 and nothing is written. The status line on the page is the plan item, which re-renders from the page JSON, so it needs no write of its own.

post.summary: Do Next Phase: ask the Claude door for a report on the plan's next phase, as a job
post.description: Reads the plan page on this site and chooses its next phase, the first with an unticked checkpoint, or the phase named. The content is the plan rendered as markdown, the phase's heading and checkpoints marked out, the SKILL.md of fedwiki-plan and of each skill the plan's status item names on a SKILLS line (read from ~/.claude/skills on the machine the farm runs on; one it cannot find is skipped with a note), and the pages the plan links on this site, the answers to its open questions first, up to 120 kB; the questions are read from the plan and from the page it links as Open Questions on this site. The model is the farm's choice (CLAUDE_DOOR_MODEL, else AUDIONOTE_SUMMARY_MODEL, else claude-opus-5-5), reached through @fortyfoxes/wiki-claude-door: the Claude API where the farm holds a key, otherwise the Claude Code CLI as whoever is logged in on the farm's machine, with every tool disallowed and a seven-minute limit. The model is asked for a fixed shape: a one-paragraph summary; one section per checkpoint of the phase saying what to do, how to verify it and whether the pages already show it done; and a closing # Proposed Ticks section listing verbatim the checkpoints it judges done, or none. The result is kept in the job; nothing is written to the plan or any page. The run holds the farm WIP marker (~/.wiki-hosting/AGENT-WIP.json, the wiki-wip protocol) from the call until the model has answered or failed, with a note naming it (Plan Tool: Do Next Phase <site>/<slug> phase N) and a heartbeat every minute, and releases it in every case; a live claim by anyone else is answered with 409 naming the holder, and nothing is started.

post.summary: Revise Plan: ask the Claude door to redraft the plan given its answered questions, as a job
post.description: Reads the plan page on this site. The content is the plan rendered as markdown, the SKILL.md of fedwiki-plan and of each skill the plan's status item names on a SKILLS line (read from ~/.claude/skills on the machine the farm runs on; one it cannot find is skipped with a note), and the pages the plan links on this site, the answers to its open questions first, up to 120 kB; the questions are read from the plan and from the page it links as Open Questions on this site. The model is the farm's choice (CLAUDE_DOOR_MODEL, else AUDIONOTE_SUMMARY_MODEL, else claude-opus-5-5), reached through @fortyfoxes/wiki-claude-door: the Claude API where the farm holds a key, otherwise the Claude Code CLI as whoever is logged in on the farm's machine, with every tool disallowed and a seven-minute limit. The model is asked to redraft the whole plan in the house format (one heading level, # Phase N with a > strap line, - [ ] checkpoints one per line, Open Questions as red question links), keeping every tick that exists and changing only what the answers justify, and to end with a # What Changed section. The redraft is kept in the job and nothing is written: the tool opens it as a ghost with the plan's own title, carrying the plan's opener, its plan item second, the redrafted body and the plan's own timeline, Assets and See unchanged, and Save over the plan (save-revision.json) writes it. The run holds the farm WIP marker (~/.wiki-hosting/AGENT-WIP.json, the wiki-wip protocol) from the call until the model has answered or failed, with a note naming it (Plan Tool: Revise Plan <site>/<slug>) and a heartbeat every minute, and releases it in every case; a live claim by anyone else is answered with 409 naming the holder, and nothing is started.

post.summary: Revise Site: ask the Claude door for a Revision Proposal for the whole site, given the answered questions, as a job
post.description: Reads the plan page on this site and its open questions, from the plan and from the page it links as Open Questions, and refuses with 400 until at least one has an answer page. The content is every answered question's page first, then every page on the site in sitemap order, the plan among them, each rendered as markdown, up to 120 kB; a page past the budget goes in as its title and first paragraph, and the account says which. Answer pages lead and are not repeated; the Open Questions page, pages whose journal forks from or credits another site, and earlier revision proposals are left out and named to the model as untouched. The model is the farm's choice (CLAUDE_DOOR_MODEL, else AUDIONOTE_SUMMARY_MODEL, else claude-opus-5-5), reached through @fortyfoxes/wiki-claude-door as Do Next Phase reaches it. It is asked for a Revision Proposal in exactly four parts: # The tone shift, two or three sentences; # Pages, one table Page | Action | Reason with Action one of Keep, Amend, Rewrite or New, in the order the revision should run, the plan last; # Untouched, each page it will not touch and why; and # Names, every personal name, place name or venue in the answer pages as an unticked - [ ] Name — Answer Page line, meaning not confirmed to travel. The proposal is kept in the job, titled Revision Proposal (dated when that page exists); the client opens it as a ghost page with Go Ahead and Pause, and nothing is written to any page. The run holds the farm WIP marker (~/.wiki-hosting/AGENT-WIP.json, the wiki-wip protocol) from the call until the model has answered or failed, with a note naming it (Plan Tool: Revise Site <site>/<slug>) and a heartbeat every minute, and releases it in every case; a live claim by anyone else is answered with 409 naming the holder, and nothing is started.

post.summary: Go Ahead: rewrite the pages a saved Revision Proposal names, one at a time through the Claude door, the plan last, as a job
post.description: Reads the saved proposal page on this site and refuses with 400 if it has no Page | Action | Reason table or says it has been applied. The plan is the one given, else the first plan the proposal links. Under the farm WIP marker, held for the whole run with the note plan: revise site <site> and a heartbeat every minute, each row is decided: Keep is skipped; Amend, Rewrite and New are done in the table's order, the plan last; and, whatever the table says, a page is never deleted and these are never written, each refusal named in the account: an answer page, the Open Questions page, a page whose journal forks from or credits another site, a page listed under Untouched, a revision proposal, a row whose page does not exist unless it asks for New. For each page the door is given the proposal's tone shift and that page's row, the answer pages, the page as it stands with each item that is not markdown shown as a keep line, the house rules (headings # with a > strap, no title heading, every wikilink kept, # See last) and the names not yet confirmed. The reply becomes the page's story: markdown items one per paragraph, heading or bullet, pipe tables as table items, and every item that is not markdown (table, timeline, diagram, assets, audio, the plan's status line) brought back whole by its id, never dropped. A page whose reply carries a name still unticked under # Names on the proposal, and that the page did not carry before, is not written: name not confirmed. Each page is written whole (temp file and rename) with journal entries as the wiki shapes them, remove, add, edit and move, each with the provenance Revised by the Plan Tool (Revise Site) from <proposal>, drawing on: <answer pages>; a New page gets a create. The plan's markdown asset is re-rendered after the plan. The proposal gains a closing line saying it was applied, and the site's index is reset. The account lists each page written with its bytes before and after and its journal entries, each refused with why, each failed, and each kept.

get.summary: How a Do Next Phase, Revise Plan, Revise Site or Go Ahead run is getting on, and its report when done
get.description: Answers { status: 'running' | 'done' | 'failed', result?, error?, started, finished } with the run's kind, plan, phase, report title, model, the account of what went to the model (skills loaded and skipped, pages, bytes) and the WIP claim's times. result is { markdown, model, ms, reportTitle, proposedTicks?, proposal? }. A Go Ahead run (kind apply) answers progress { n, of, title } while it runs and an account of every page written (bytes before and after, the journal entries), refused (and why), failed and kept; its result is the counts. Jobs are kept in the farm's handler process and mirrored to status/farm-tmp/plan-jobs/<id>.json; one found only on disk and still marked running is answered as failed, since the process that ran it is gone. Declared as a write so only someone who may edit the site reads a report on its plan. Another site's job is not found.

post.summary: Finish Plan: write the Conclusion section and the demo link once every checkpoint is ticked
post.description: Reads the plan page on this site and refuses with 400 unless every phase checkpoint is ticked (the Open Questions are not phases), a conclusion is given, and the demo title names a page that exists on this site or on a sibling site of this farm. It then writes, in place, a # Conclusion section immediately above the # See section (the fedwiki-plan end matter: body, Files, Links, Assets, Conclusion, See), or at the end when there is no See: the heading item # Conclusion, the conclusion one markdown item per paragraph, and a closing line The demo is [[<demo>]]. An existing Conclusion section has its body replaced, item by item. - [[<demo>]] is added to the See list unless the section already links it. Each item is journaled as an add or an edit (a remove for a surplus old body item), shaped as the wiki journals them; the page is written whole (temp file and rename); the site's sitemap.json, site-index.json and sitemap.xml are removed together so it reindexes; and the plan's markdown is re-rendered to assets/<slug>/<slug>.md. The write holds the farm WIP marker (~/.wiki-hosting/AGENT-WIP.json, the wiki-wip protocol) with a note naming it and releases it; a live claim by anyone else is answered with 409 and nothing is written.

post.summary: Save over the plan: write the Revise Plan ghost's story over the plan in place, journaled, the old version its _rev
post.description: Takes the story of the ghost Revise Plan opened, with the plan's own title. Its first item, the line saying it is a proposed revision, is dropped; the rest must carry a plan item. The story is written over the plan with reviseJournal: a remove for each item gone, an add or edit for each new or changed one, a move for each out of place, so the version it replaces is /view/<slug>_rev<N>. Under the farm WIP marker the plan is read again; a page forked from or credited to another site is refused. When a script wrote the page without journal entries, entries that bring the journal level with the story it holds are appended first, so the previous rev is exactly the page as it was. The page as it was is written to the site's recycler (recycle/<slug>, where the wiki's own fork saves a page it replaces), the plan is written whole (temp file and rename), every entry carrying a provenance and a planTool field the status line reads, the plan's markdown asset is re-rendered to assets/<slug>/<slug>.md and the site's index files are removed so it reindexes. Before writing, the journal is replayed: it must give back the old story at the previous rev and the new story at the end, or nothing is written.

post.summary: Red-link: research each of the plan's red links on the web and write its page, as a job
post.description: Reads the plan page on this site and collects its links: [[wikilinks]] in markdown, paragraph and html items (outside ``` fences) and timeline event labels. A link is red when no page with its slug is on any site of this farm or of the farms named in WIKI_EXTRA_FARMS, and it is not one of the installed plugins' own pages. Question links (a title ending in ?) and everything under the # Open Questions heading are never written: a page behind a question marks it answered, and that is a person's act. Up to 6 red links a run are taken one at a time. For each, the Claude door is asked, through the Claude Code CLI with WebSearch and WebFetch and no other tool, to research it from its primary sources and write its page in full; the page is written at once as a new page on this site, the name as its makers write it, opening with a line saying it is AI generated and researched on the web for this plan, commands as terminal items, a Links section of sources and a See section back to the plan, with a journal of one create carrying its provenance. A page whose slug exists anywhere on the farm by then is skipped, never overwritten. The job's progress names the page in hand; its result lists the pages written, skipped and failed, and meta how many red links remain and the questions left alone. 400 when the plan has no red links. The run holds the farm WIP marker, named Plan Tool: Red-link <site>/<slug>. An untouched stub of Red-link's own on this site (one create in its journal, with Red-link's stub provenance) counts as still missing: it is researched and written over the stub through the journal, the stub kept as rev0; a stub anyone has edited is left alone.
